posts.author: Abhishek Mishra
posts.title: The Art of Procedural Generation in Games
posts.content: As a game developer and artist, I'm fascinated by procedural generation. It's not just about creating endless worlds; it's about designing a *system* that can build a unique experience for every player. The real challenge is teaching the code what 'looks good' or 'feels right'. That's where the art and the programming truly merge.

posts.author: Reia Baid
posts.title: Why Your Website Needs to be Accessible
posts.content: In frontend development, we often focus on the visual 'wow' factor. But what if a user can't see your site? Or can't use a mouse? Web accessibility (a11y) means building our sites so *everyone* can use them. This includes using proper HTML, making sites keyboard-navigable, and ensuring color contrast. It's not just a 'nice-to-have', it's a core part of being a good developer.

posts.author: Abhijeet Gupta
posts.title: Good Design is Invisible: A UX Deep Dive
posts.content: Have you ever used an app that just... worked? You found everything you needed without thinking? That's the power of good User Experience (UX) design. Our job as designers isn't to add more features; it's to remove friction. We use tools like Figma to build prototypes and test flows *before* any code is written. This saves time and ensures the final product is built for the user, not for us.
